speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the consultation. I am Dr. Agent; I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress. To begin my assessment, could you tell me how long this difficulty breathing has been occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Given the prematurity and cesarean delivery, was the baby delivered via forceps or vacuum, and do you know if there were any complications during labor or delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN).

Based on your prematurity, cesarean delivery, and the classic signs of retained fetal lung fluid like tachypnea, retractions, and nasal flaring, this clinical picture strongly points to TTN. I am ready to proceed with a Chest_X-Ray to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes like pneumonia.
